module_title: Expansion of British Power - Anglo-Mysore and Anglo-Maratha Wars
introduction: After taking control of Bengal, the British faced two of the largest and most modern regional powers—Mysore and the Marathas—to establish their monopoly over Southern and Central India. This level covers these conflicts and their concluding treaties.

core_concepts.title: Anglo-Mysore Wars (1767-1799)
core_concepts.description: A series of 4 wars. Haider Ali and his son Tipu Sultan offered fierce resistance to the British. In the 4th war (1799), Tipu Sultan was martyred while defending Seringapatam, and a Subsidiary Alliance was imposed on Mysore.

core_concepts.title: Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775-1818)
core_concepts.description: A series of 3 wars. The 1st war ended in a draw (Treaty of Salbai). However, internal disunity among Maratha chiefs (Scindia, Holkar, Bhonsle) led to British victories in the 2nd and 3rd wars. In 1818, the post of 'Peshwa' was completely abolished.

core_concepts.title: Ring Fence Policy
core_concepts.description: Initiated by Warren Hastings, the objective of this policy was to defend their own territory (Bengal) by protecting the borders of neighboring states (like Awadh), essentially creating buffer zones.

core_concepts.title: Dual Government of Bengal
core_concepts.description: Implemented by Robert Clive. The British held the 'Diwani' (revenue collection rights), while the Nawab held the 'Nizamat' (administration and justice). Power was with the British, while responsibility lay with the Nawab.

core_concepts.title: Treaty of Bassein (1802)
core_concepts.description: A 'Subsidiary Alliance' signed between Peshwa Baji Rao II and the British. It is often regarded as the death knell of Maratha independence.

important_entities.name: Haider Ali
important_entities.significance: He inflicted a heavy defeat on the British in the First Anglo-Mysore War and reached the gates of Madras. He died of cancer during the Second War.

important_entities.name: Tipu Sultan
important_entities.significance: He became a member of the Jacobin Club, planted the Tree of Liberty, and modernized his army along European lines (including the use of iron-cased rockets).

important_entities.name: Warren Hastings
important_entities.significance: He abolished Robert Clive's 'Dual Government' and introduced major reforms in the judicial system.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Tipu's Role in the Mysore Wars
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Note that Tipu was not the primary ruler during the First Anglo-Mysore War. He took command midway through the Second War after his father Haider Ali's death.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: End of the First Anglo-Maratha War
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: This war did not end with the Treaty of Surat or Purandar. It ended with the historic 'Treaty of Salbai' (1782), which established peace for 20 years.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1st War: Treaty of Madras, 2nd War: Treaty of Mangalore, 3rd War: Treaty of Seringapatam.

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: Sequence of States Accepting Subsidiary Alliance
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Hyderabad (1798 - first to accept), followed by Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa, Bhonsle, Scindia.

exam_strategy_tips: Matching the treaties of the Mysore Wars (M-M-S) with their respective wars is a highly frequent question format.
A standard question: 'In which war was Tipu Sultan killed?' (Answer: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, 1799).
